title: Task intent
description: A plain-language goal pointing at the card that answers it. These exist because a beginner does not know the topic word to search for: she knows she wants to undo something, not that the word is `revert`. Intents are the bridge from her vocabulary to the corpus vocabulary, and they are the single highest-leverage retrieval artifact in the project.

goal.description: Stated as she would state it, first person, plain. 'I want to undo my last commit but keep the changes.'

phrasings.description: Every way she might ask, including the panicked and ungrammatical ones. 'oops', 'i wrecked it', 'go back', 'undo', 'take it back'. Be generous: these are cheap to write and each one is a query that now lands correctly. Include the wrong technical word she might reach for, since half of getting unstuck is not knowing the right one.

target.description: The card that actually answers it.

urgency.description: panic routes straight into the Panic surface rather than the reader. Something is broken and she does not want a lecture.
